% ---- Pandoc compatibility shims ---------------------------------------
% Pandoc emits table column specs that reference \real and \tightlist;
% these macros are provided by pandoc's default LaTeX template but not by
% the ACL style, so we declare them here. Without these, pipe-table
% conversions render as raw column-spec text in the body.
\providecommand{\real}[1]{#1}
\providecommand{\tightlist}{%
  \setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}}
% pandoc 3.x uses \pandocbounded to wrap floats; harmless no-op shim:
\providecommand{\pandocbounded}[1]{#1}

\title{What Must Be Trained and What Can Be Prompted: A Per-Capability Study of Tutor Redirect Behavior}

\author{Miles Yung \\
  Independent Research \\
  \texttt{milesyung2026@gmail.com}}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

% -------------------------------------------------------------------------
% Abstract
% -------------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{abstract}
Deploying a small language model as an English tutor forces a practical
decision: for each behavior a deployment prompt already \emph{describes}, does
an explicit prompt clause \emph{elicit} it, or must it be demonstrated through
fine-tuning? We answer this per-capability under a \textbf{matched-prompt}
protocol --- the identical fully-specified prompt given to a fine-tuned 0.8B
student and to prompt-only baselines up to a 9B teacher --- so a prompt-only
failure isolates promptability rather than under-specification.

Under the tested small-model and prompting regimes, the behaviors separate into
\emph{three} operational regimes rather than a binary. \textbf{(A)
Prompt-sufficient}: locale-leakage fidelity reaches prompt-only parity.
\textbf{(B) Prompt-elicitable but data-refinable}: role-swap and topic
re-anchoring appear prompt-only as a \emph{type}, yet specialized data wins a
pairwise quality comparison decisively (role-swap win-rate 0.87). \textbf{(C)
Training-dependent (under the tested regimes)}: multi-turn persistence (firing a
session-end sentinel on the third same-axis violation) and pedagogical
withholding are named by the prompt but not reliably elicited --- the 9B teacher
reaches \(\leq\)0.06 persistence recall zero/few-shot and 0.63 with native
chain-of-thought (below the student's 0.83, at 1.6--3.2k reasoning tokens/turn),
and withholds on under half of probes (0.45) versus the student's 0.61 (paired
tests, two judges). The regime-C effects replicate \emph{in direction} in a
trained Llama-3.2-1B student evaluated against its own untrained base
(persistence 0.25\(\to\)0.91, withholding 0.11\(\to\)0.50), separating training
from scale within a shared base; magnitude is family-dependent.

Reading the regime-A/B axes honestly required retiring the conventional
context-blind redirect-axis macro-F1 (a \emph{type} classifier that ties student
and teacher) in favor of capability-specific metrics. All experiments run on one
RTX 3060 12GB GPU; we release the apparatus and analysis scripts.
\end{abstract}
